text:
Ivan Barbashev is back on the Golden Knights' top line. "Experiment over," as the Las Vegas Review-Journal put it on Nov. 16. His minutes haven't followed yet: 14.2 a night over the last ten games, about two under his usual, with six points against 5.7 expected.

The season line is steady: 5 goals and 17 points in 25 games, 53 hits, and with him on the ice at 5v5 Vegas has 60% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality). His finishing (5 goals on 5.7 expected) and his linemates' shooting are both close to normal, so there's little luck either way.

His value comes from being where the good passes go. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him taking 1.5 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net last season; those shots go in 25% of the time, against 6% when the shooter makes his own play. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 42nd among 401 forwards at 2.2 wins above replacement, with the note that strong linemates flatter his raw numbers.

What to watch: whether the top-line job brings his ice time back up.
